doc.title: Rob Mounsey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 9, 2025

title: Money, digital plug-ins and home recording
summary: He was never motivated by money; analog gear gave way to software, and musicians now overdub from home, as Randy Brecker and Steve Khan do.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: And did you then make a concerted effort to redirect your talents to wherever the money might be?

I was never motivated by money. I have to admit, yes, to the occasional disapproval of some family members I just wasn’t motivated by money. The synth thing went a little bit out of style but also the technology meant that all of that analog equipment kind of became replaced by digital plug-ins, and now I have a set-up which is quite small and simple with loads of software. So that technology changed a lot. And if people want me to overdub sounds on their production they can just email files to me, I’ll do it in my own little place and send them back. And that happens pretty often. I know a lot of studio musicians that, especially guitarists for some reason, they become very adept at home recording. And guitarists, you know they have not only 17 different guitars but also every kind of guitar-like instrument, the ukuleles and the Mexican cuatros and the baglama saz and the Brazilian, you know

Cavaquinhos and the different banjos, the tenor banjo, the five string banjo, the pedal steel. And so they collect the microphones and the pre-amps and they can do everything at home now and a lot of playing musicians are very, very adept at all of that and they can do great work at home.
I know Randy Brecker mentioned that, things in the mail and overdubbed solos.

Yeah he does quite a lot of that. I’ve done that with him with my buddy Steve Khan, guitarist. Steve and Randy are close and I know Randy well. Steve is a buddy of mine. And Bob Mintzer I think is another one.
